column7:
Are you an Example College student, alum or staff member? 

NOTE: Only Example College students, alumni and staff may sell at Example Makers Fair.

If you are not, you are welcome to visit the fair as a shopper.
column8: Please give your Example College email address. Alumni and staff may give the address the college gave them, even if they no longer use it often.
column9: If you have no Example College email, please upload something that shows you study or work at Example College, such as a class timetable or a staff card.
column10:
Discord username

The fair's team talks to vendors on Discord: your table, your set-up time and any change on the day all come through it. Please give the username we can find you by, and join the server when we invite you.

(your username, not your display name)
column12: Link to your business (a shop, a website or a page)
column13: Have you sold your work at a market or fair before?
column14: What will you be selling at the fair?
column15:
If you plan to sell rings, which sizes will you bring? 

A range is fine; leave this blank if you are not selling rings.
column16: Please upload one short video of you making a piece of your work, so the review team can see it is made by hand (a phone video is fine).
column17: Please upload any sketches or work-in-progress photos of the pieces you will bring.
column18:
Please share a link to your portfolio or to photos of what you will bring to Example Makers Fair.

A website, a social page or a shared folder all work, as long as it shows recent pieces.

If it is private, please let anyone with the link view it until applications close.

We look at every portfolio, and the more of your current work it shows, the easier it is for us to say yes. 

Please do not send a link that asks us to sign in.
column19:
I confirm that everything I sell at the fair is designed and made by me.

Resold, dropshipped and traced work is not allowed, and the team may ask a vendor selling it to pack up and leave.

Fan art is welcome, as long as the drawing is your own.
column20:
Example Makers Fair's mission is to give student and alumni makers a first place to sell their work. 

Tables go first to makers who have not sold at many markets before. 

I have read the fair's mission and agree to support it.
column21:
I confirm that everything in this application is true and that it is my own.

An application made for someone else, or copied from another, will not be considered.
column22:
I confirm that my work follows the fair's content rules.

Families walk through the fair, so:

- No work showing graphic violence or sexual content. 
- No work aimed at a person or a group of people.
- Keep work for an older audience in a closed binder, and ask for ID first.
- If you are unsure about a piece, ask the team on Discord before the fair.
column23: Which clubs are you part of?
column24: If you are in one of these clubs, please upload proof of membership.
column25:
Which tables would you take on each day of the fair? Tick both tiers if either works for you.

NOTE: 
- Gold tables face the front entrance of Example Hall; Silver tables are in the North Wing and cost a little less.
- Leave a day at None if you cannot be there, and we will not give you a table that day.
- The more days and tiers you tick, the better your chance of a table. [Monday, April 20]

column31:
Do you want a half table or full table?

- A half table is half the width and half the fee of a full table.
- Half tables are shared with another vendor.
- Choose Either if you are happy with whichever we have room for.
- We cannot change your table size after results are out.
column32:
If you chose half table or either, who would you like to share with?

Give their email address as they wrote it on their own application.

NOTE:
- Each of you must apply on your own.
- Your partner must also choose a half table or either.
- Leave this blank and we will pair you with another vendor where we can.
- We try to keep every pair together but cannot promise it.
